prompt: Why does Quicksort hit Θ(n²) on already-sorted input when using the first element as pivot?
options: Because comparisons take longer on sorted data
Because the pivot is always the minimum, producing maximally unbalanced partitions
Because Quicksort cannot handle sorted input at all
Because Merge Sort would be used instead
explanation: With sorted input and first-element pivot, every partition splits into one empty side and one side of size n-1, giving recursion depth n.

prompt: Run Merge Sort on [8, 3, 5, 1, 9, 2]. Give the final sorted array as JSON.
explanation: Merge Sort recursively splits the array in half and merges sorted halves back together.

prompt: Run Quicksort on [6, 1, 8, 3, 5]. Give the final sorted array as JSON.
explanation: Quicksort partitions around a pivot (first element of the region), then recursively sorts each side.

prompt: What is the asymptotic lower bound for ANY comparison-based sorting algorithm's worst case?
explanation: From the decision-tree argument: log₂(n!) = Θ(n log n) comparisons are needed in the worst case.
